newsitem.title: UK: BA to discuss co-operation deal with Iberia.
newsitem.headline: BA to discuss co-operation deal with Iberia.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Friday it had signed a memorandum of understanding committing it to discussing a co-operation deal with Spanish flag carrier Iberia.
British Airways also said that it was evaluating taking a minority equity stake in Iberia, which the Spanish government intends to privatise.

The talks will initially focus on a marketing agreement to provide benefits to the airlines' customers on flights beyond London and Madrid, as well as "reciprocal participation in their frequent flyer programmes," BA said in a statement.

The carrier said that marketing co-operation could later cover a wider range of routes and the airlines hope to extend any partnership to other areas where cost savings can be made. They are also looking at co-ordinating cargo operations.

The two airlines will also discuss the possibility of Iberia participating in BA's other alliances, including its proposed alliance with American Airlines. That alliance, announced just over a year ago, has been held up by regulatory authorities in the UK, Europe and the United States, as well as over talks about a new Anglo-U.S. aviation trade agreement.
BA said the agreement should come into effect next summer.

"This commercial agreement would offer both our and Iberia's customers considerable advantages, in particular by making it easier to fly to a wider range of destinations," said Bob Ayling, BA's chief executive.
